title: introduce-regional-failover-controlplane-peering-with-ephemeral-route-targets-and-dns-sync
author: Priya N. Iyer
description: Context: Private control plane installations in multi-region accounts occasionally experience cross-account DNS resolution failures during regional failover. This PR introduces a deterministic regional-fallback peering mechanism that creates ephemeral route targets and orchestrates conditional Route53 Resolver rule promotion for the control plane's private hosted zones. Motivation: reduce downtime during regional control plane migrations and simplify cross-account endpoint routing without permanently enlarging peering footprints. Design summary: (1) Terraform module `controlplane-peering` creates scoped peering connections with tags and a lifecycle policy that ensures peering attachments are ephemeral and self-reconciling; (2) Helm hooks for the private controlplane operator to trigger staged DNS promotion and graceful KV-cache flushing when peering target changes; (3) Add a resolver-guard Lambda (optional) that validates resolver rules and applies TTL-aware promotion to preserve DNS cache correctness; (4) Security: security group templates restrict controlplane peering to specific ports and use egress-only prefix lists for data plane egress; (5) Rollout: a canary rollout that first provisions peering and resolver rules in the staging account, then promotes to two additional regions with automatic rollback on health/trace regressions. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module and example usage - [x] Helm chart templates and hook implementations - [x] IAM least-privilege for peering orchestration - [x] E2E canary test in staging - [x] Observability: metrics + alerts for resolver promotion failures - [x] Upgrade and rollback documentation included in the chart notes. Testing and validation: unit tests for Terraform plan diffs added under modules/controlplane-peering/tests; integration harness run against the staging org with three accounts verified resolver promotion under 95th percentile latency. Manual runbooks for forced rollback are added: `docs/rollback-controlplane-peering.md`. Deployment notes: Use the new chart values `controlplane.peering.enabled=true` and `controlplane.peering.fallbackRegions=["us-west-2","us-east-1"]`. When enabling in production, first run the terraform module with `plan-only` in a non-prod account to inspect proposed peering attachments. If the optional resolver-guard Lambda is enabled, ensure the IAM role is granted cross-account Route53Resolver permissions. Related: ENG-6372 for rollout automation, OPS-129 for incident follow-ups.

review_comments: Marco Li: This looks good overall. Two asks: 1) Can we make the resolver-guard optional by default? 2) Add a smoke test that verifies SRV/TXT records are preserved during promotion.
Priya N. Iyer: Agree; made resolver-guard opt-in via chart value `resolverGuard.enabled=false` by default and added an integration smoke test validating TXT preservation.

Priya N. Iyer: Applied SG change and added threat model section to docs/rollback-controlplane-peering.md.

release_notes: Add optional regional-failover peering for private control planes. Includes terraform module, helm chart hooks, resolver promotion tooling, and rollback runbook. Opt-in via chart values. No breaking changes by default.
notes_for_ops: To enable: run terraform apply in a non-prod account first. Ensure cross-account IAM roles exist before enabling resolver guard. Canary duration defaults to 30 minutes; extend if you have long TTL caches.
incident_related: This PR addresses repeated incidents of controlplane DNS mismatch during region failover (see SUP-4412).
testing_summary: Unit tests for module diffs, helm-lint, and staging canary integration. Manual rollback tested end-to-end using the provided runbook. Observability: added metric resolver_promotion.success and resolver_promotion.latency.
